undergoing [[language revival|revival]]{{cite web | url=https://www.sharkbay.org/culture-history/aboriginal-heritage/aboriginal-languages/ | title=Aboriginal Languages }} | altname = Malkana }} '''Malgana''', also known as '''Malkana''', is the [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Aboriginal Australian language]] of the [[Malgana people]] of [[Western Australia]]. It is one of the [[Kartu languages]] of the [[Pama–Nyungan languages|Pama–Nyungan family]] of languages. The Irra Wangga Language Centre (having taken over from the Yamaji Language Centre) has been carrying out work on the Malgana language since 1995, and has produced an illustrated wordlist from local speakers of the language. ''A Sketch Grammar of Malgana'' (Gargett, 2012) was published by Pacific Linguistics.{{cite web | title=Irra Wangga | website=Bundiyarra | url=https://www.bundiyarra.com/irrawangga | access-date=22 October 2023}} There is a sign in the [[Shire of Shark Bay]] that reads {{lang|vml|Yandani Gathaagudu}}, with under it being the [[English language|English]] translation, "Welcome to Shark Bay".{{cite news | url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2023-10-22/malgana-aboriginal-language-workshops-shark-bay-wa/102973752 | title=Bob wasn't allowed to speak his language growing up.
